Pre-Xmas Party plan

A Canadian summer barbecue in December — Waterloo alumni and friends from across the Greater Bay Area (Hong Kong, Macao, Shenzhen and beyond), gathered at a container farm in Kam Tin for BBQ, free-flow drinks and Beer Olympics, plus the first announcement of the February 2027 70th Anniversary Gala.

01

The afternoon itself

No fixed schedule — people eat, drink, play and drift between the patio, the garden and the containers. Announcements (including the Gala reveal) happen when there's a natural crowd.

Eat & drink

Canadian BBQ buffet

Barbecue buffet with free-flow alcohol, in the spirit of a Canadian summer cookout. Site access, food, drinks and cutlery are all inside the HK$400-per-person package.

Optional extra under discussion: custom wine via Michael or his contact.

Play

Beer Olympics

Teams of 3–4, each with its own team cheer. Flip cup and boat racing run outdoors on the patio; beer pong is played indoors only — see the container layout in section 04.

Announce

70th Anniversary Gala

The party doubles as the launch moment for the University of Waterloo's 70th Anniversary Gala in February 2027 — first public announcement to the Hong Kong chapter community.

Pricing & the UW subsidy

The venue package costs HK$400 per person — site access, food, drinks, cutlery and everything in between. What a guest pays depends on their affiliation, below.

− HK$100

Michael has approved a HK$100-per-person subsidy for anyone affiliated with the University of Waterloo in any way — alumni, exchange students, co-op students and more. UW-affiliated guests therefore pay HK$300, not the HK$400 cost. The subsidy applies only to UW-affiliated guests — everyone else pays the full HK$400. UW places are no longer free.

Event day
04

Beer Olympics — and why pong stays indoors

Teams of 3–4, a team cheer each, and a running bracket on the scoreboard. Two of the three games live outdoors; beer pong does not — loose balls on the patio would be lost in the garden within minutes and end up polluting the farm, so pong is played inside the containers.

Outdoors · Patio

Flip cup

Relay drinking-and-flipping on the long patio tables. No loose balls, nothing to lose in the grass. How flip cup works ↗

Outdoors · Patio

Boat racing

Head-to-head team chugging relay — loud, fast, and the best spectator game of the three. How boat racing works ↗

Indoors only · Containers

Beer pong

Played inside 20-foot containers, never outdoors: stray balls outdoors would be lost and pollute the farm. Inside, every bounce stays in the box and gets picked up. How beer pong works ↗

One table per container — the layout that fits

A 20-foot TEU container is about 5.89 m long × 2.35 m wide inside. A regulation beer pong table is 2.44 m × 0.61 m. Set lengthwise down the middle, it leaves roughly 1.7 m of standing room at each end for players and about 0.87 m clear on each side — so two tables means two containers, and spectators watch from the open door end.

Net across the doorwayThe open doors are the one escape route left for balls — a net or curtain keeps them in while air still flows.
Spectators at the door endSide clearance is for players stepping back, not a crowd. The scoreboard sits at the door so everyone can follow the bracket.
Light, air & a mopEach game container needs lighting, airflow, and a bin and mop inside — spilt beer in an enclosed box gets noticeable fast.
05

The games kit — the farm's investment, not the party budget

For MVF: the Beer Olympics equipment is bought, owned and stored by Movertical Farm as a reusable investment for future events. It does not come out of the HK$400-per-person party package. The chapter is helping the farm budget and plan the kit — this is the proposed list to price and approve.
Buy once · Reusable core kit

What the farm buys and keeps

  • 2 folding beer pong tables — regulation 2.44 m × 0.61 m; two tables (in two containers) let matches run in parallel, and they double as flip cup tables.
  • ~100 sturdy plastic cups — 20 game cups + rinse cups per pong table, one per player for flip cup and boat racing, plus spares for cracks.
  • 24 pong balls — only 2–3 in play per table; the rest are spares. Balls are always the first thing to disappear.
  • Scoreboard — whiteboard and markers for the bracket, team names and cheers; reusable for any future tournament.
  • Team markers in 5 colours — bandanas, sashes or bibs, 4–5 per colour, so teams stay recognisable in photos.
  • 1–2 labelled storage bins — lidded, with an inventory list inside the lid, so the whole kit is findable for the next event.
Per event · Small top-up

What gets restocked each time

  • Replacement balls & cracked cups — top up to the core counts above; expect a handful of each per event.
  • Fresh whiteboard markers — they dry out between events like nothing else.
  • Cleaning — wash and air the cups, bibs and tables before the kit goes back in its bins.

With ~20 guests in teams of 3–4 (about 5 teams), the core kit runs a proper tournament by rotation — and it keeps working well beyond 20. If much larger groups become regular, the sensible next buy is another pair of tables, once demand is proven.

06

The venue & getting there

About Movertical Farm

MVF is an innovative research centre combining aquaponics — aquaculture and hydroponics together — with intermodal shipping containers. The site has a patio, a barbecue pit, an agricultural garden, and a run of containers fitted out for entertainment: lounge, karaoke, massage chairs and more.

Capacity is well over a hundred people, so our expected ~20 will have room to spread out — and room to grow if invitations travel further than expected.

MVF website ↗ Open in Maps ↗

Getting there

  • MTR to Kam Sheung Road — the nearest station to the farm.
  • Minibus 601B to Shui Mei Tsuen — from Kam Sheung Road station, then a short walk to MVF.
  • Party hours 15:00–20:00 — daylight for the garden and games, evening for the patio lights and announcements.

Full directions are in the Maps link — worth sending to guests with the invitation, as Kam Tin is new territory for most Hong Kong islanders.
